messages:
alex (PM): quick triage — two customer asks landed that touch GA acceptance: 1) guaranteed burst capacity for Dedicated, 2) 1yr audit log retention for Private. both could change SLA/pricing. can we sync?
maya (Eng): available. need to know exact burst QPS and retention edges. both are non-trivial.
sam (SRE): +1. burst guarantees mean capacity reservations or hard limits. impacts autoscaler and cost.
jordan (Support): support implications: longer log retention increases storage + longer debug windows. ops runbook needs updates for escalations on burst failures.
frances (Sales): customers are strategic — one will only sign if burst SLA included. they'd pay for it. prefer to capture as add-on.
leo (FinOps): if we promise burst SLA at GA we need pricing delta. rough calc: reserved burst + buffer = ~1.6x baseline cost. we should gate on committed spend.
maya (Eng): engineering tradeoffs: 1) soft-burst (best-effort) — cheap, no SLA; 2) reserved-burst (strict) — requires capacity pool + admission control + metrics. reserved-burst will add code + infra changes. ETA: 6w for basic admission control + 2w for e2e testing.
sam (SRE): for SLA math we need to define failure modes. is burst SLA about latency under load or total request acceptance? both change monitoring.
alex (PM): good point. let's be specific: customer asks for "burst capacity to sustain 2x baseline QPS for 10 min with <200ms p95". they want formal SLA.
jordan (Support): that latency target needs runbook playbook: when we hit degraded burst, auto-fallback to model variant + notify customer. need docs.
frances (Sales): propose we offer 'Burst Assurance' as a paid feature: 1) capacity commit threshold, 2) uplifted price, 3) routing priority. keeps GA surface smaller.
maya (Eng): feasible as paid add-on. for GA we can ship best-effort bursting + doc that paid tier adds admission control and SLA.
leo (FinOps): pricing phrasing suggestion: "Burst Assurance: reserved capacity billed monthly; 1.6x baseline unit cost for burst window". need legal to review.
sam (SRE): audit logs: 1yr retention has implications on storage and retrieval performance. we already support 90d retention as default. 1yr requires lifecycle policies and possibly cold storage.
alex (PM): can we scope audit retention as follow: GA: 90d default, 1yr as "Compliance Add-on" for Private with explicit pricing and deployment checklist?
maya (Eng): yes. implementation plan: add configurable retention in storage service, migration job for existing logs, UI toggle + infra flags. dev effort ~3w.
jordan (Support): support will need access controls doc + runbook for retrieval requests (SLA on retrieval).
frances (Sales): that maps cleanly to customers needing compliance. prefer to keep GA clean and push 1yr as add-on.
leo (FinOps): thumbs up. we should model revenue vs cost by customer size — will share a spreadsheet tomorrow.
sam (SRE): monitoring checklist for GA if we keep baseline (no burst SLA):
```
- alert: sustained CPU/GPU utilization >85% for 5m
- alert: p95 latency >200ms for 5m
- synthetic job every 1m across regions
- oncall runbook: scale path + fallback to model variant
```
maya (Eng): add: metric for admission-control rejections (if we implement reserved pool).
alex (PM): proposed GA acceptance decisions (draft):
1) Baseline SLA: 99.9% regional availability, baseline latency SLO doc (p50/p95), 90d audit logs.
2) Burst Assurance: not in GA baseline — available as paid add-on with reserved capacity and SLA.
3) Compliance Logs 1yr: not in GA baseline — Private add-on with deployment checklist.
4) Docs + Support: GA must include rollout runbook, escalation ladder, and sample customer contract language for both add-ons.
5) Observability: synthetic tests + runbook alerts in place.

frances (Sales): sounds reasonable. need sample contract language ASAP to close deal.
jordan (Support): I'll draft runbook skeleton and sample escalation steps by EOD.
maya (Eng): engineering action items: admission-control prototype (spike) for burst: 2w spike, then implementation if green. retention config PR planned in sprints next 3 weeks.
sam (SRE): oncall changes: add new paging policy for burst incidents and update SLO burn charts. I'll update runbook once Jordan posts skeleton.
leo (FinOps): I'll post cost model + recommended price bands tomorrow.
alex (PM): decisions captured: GA baseline keeps scope tight. Burst and 1yr logs are add-ons. Owners: Maya (eng lead) for burst, Sam (SRE) for monitoring/oncall, Jordan (Support) for runbook, Leo (FinOps) for pricing, Frances (Sales) to validate contract language. Action: brief stakeholders in partner meeting Friday.
frances (Sales): I'll route the draft contract language to legal after I get the sample.
deploy-bot: scheduled -> doc: "GA-acceptance-decision-log" created by alex at 4315123620
alex (PM): thanks team — small follow-up: can everyone add 1-line status to the doc by tomorrow noon? keeps Friday sync tight. :thumbsup:
